passage: The shop would shut in fifteen minutes, rain was hammering the awning, and Papa had money for exactly one new school bag. "Vidya, take the blue one. You've earned it." Her brother Raghav, standing beside her with his torn strap knotted at the corner, said nothing. Vidya felt a warm glow, and then a twist in her stomach. That same afternoon Papa had proudly told the shopkeeper about her science fair prize. She turned to the shopkeeper. "Actually, Raghav built half the model. He did the wiring." Papa blinked. "Did he? Then Raghav, choose one too," he said, counting again. "We'll check for a smaller one." Raghav looked up, surprised and shy. Vidya let out a breath she hadn't known she was holding.

qa.q: How much time was left before the shop shut?
qa.a: Fifteen minutes were left before the shop shut.

qa.q: What was Vidya feeling as she held the blue bag while Raghav stood beside her?
qa.a: She felt warm about being valued but uneasy, because she noticed that Raghav's strap was knotted and he said nothing.

qa.q: What did Vidya do that used her favoured position kindly?
qa.a: She shared credit by telling her father and the shopkeeper that Raghav built half the model, instead of enjoying all the praise. 😊

qa.q: How might Raghav have felt when Vidya spoke up?
qa.a: Probably surprised and shy, and maybe relieved, since his work was finally mentioned and his father offered him a bag too.

grounding: Shows a favoured teen feeling warm but uneasy, aware her sibling is left out, who shares credit instead of exploiting her status.

passage:
Preeti, you asked why I always call your Suresh Chacha first when I have good news. Here is why.
When we were boys in Solapur, I, Chaitanya, was Baba's favourite. I had his face, his love of numbers, his loud laugh. When I topped the district exam, Baba bought laddoos for the whole lane and called me "my lion." Suresh, one year younger, stood at the back holding the plates.
I felt warm, and uneasy too. I saw him eat alone on the step.
That evening the headmaster came to congratulate me. I could have taken all the praise. Instead I said, "Suresh drilled me with questions every night for a month." It was true. Baba turned and looked at Suresh properly, maybe for the first time that year.
After that I made a rule for myself: never take a prize without naming who helped. And never let Suresh stand at the back again.

qa.q: What did Baba buy when young Chaitanya topped the district exam?
How did young Chaitanya feel when Baba called him 'my lion'?
qa.a: He felt warm and proud, yet uneasy, because he noticed Suresh standing at the back and eating alone.

qa.q: What was the turning point when the headmaster came, and why did it matter?
qa.a: Chaitanya chose to share the credit by saying Suresh had drilled him every night, which made Baba finally notice Suresh.

qa.q: How might young Suresh have felt holding the plates at the back?
qa.a: Suresh probably felt left out and invisible, watching his brother celebrated while his own help went unseen.

grounding: An elder recalls being the favourite child, feeling uneasy about his brother's pain, and choosing to share credit instead of enjoying the status.

passage:
The results came out at seven, right as the power went. With only Nilesh's phone charged, the whole family crowded around its glow on the dark verandah.
"Ninety-three!" Aai hugged Nilesh so tightly his glasses slipped. Baba was already calling relatives. Nobody asked about Usha, whose Class 10 results had come out the same evening.
Nilesh felt the warmth, and also Usha's silence beside him. She had eighty-one. He knew because she'd shown him first, quietly, before the lights died.
"Usha got eighty-one," he said loudly. "And she's the one who explained all of trigonometry to me. Half this ninety-three is hers."
Aai paused. Baba lowered his phone.
When the neighbour sent over a box of pedas, Nilesh put the box in Usha's lap. "You open it," he said. Usha looked at him in the candlelight and, slowly, smiled.

qa.q: How did Nilesh feel when Aai hugged him and nobody asked about Usha?
qa.a: He felt warm but uneasy and guilty, aware of Usha's hurt silence beside him.

qa.q: What small steps did Nilesh take to avoid exploiting his favoured place?
qa.a: He announced Usha's marks, credited her help with trigonometry, and handed her the box of pedas to open.

qa.q: What is it like for Usha when the family crowds around Nilesh?
qa.a: She likely feels overlooked and hurt, since her own results came the same evening and nobody asked about them.

grounding: A favoured teen feels warm but uneasy as his sister is overlooked, and shares credit and attention with her.
